title: the retired vibelang:flows specifier owns nothing: it is an ordinary unresolvable foreign module, not the durable intrinsic
notes: docs/DECISIONS.md (Locked): '`smithers:flows` is a compiler-owned virtual module', and specification/durable-execution.mdx:24: '`durable` is a compiler-recognized function imported from the compiler-owned `smithers:flows` virtual module.' Exactly one specifier is named, so any other spelling is an ordinary module specifier and is subject to the ordinary rules — here, an unresolvable one, which is an untrusted foreign module edge (SMITHERS1510 at the specifier). The retired spelling is the interesting one because the Go bridge carried it in both `compilerModuleSpecifiers` and `durableModuleSpecifiers`, so this exact program compiled there, contributed no requirement, did not block a native pin, and lowered `durable(...)` into a real digest-pinned Plan — a language name that no longer exists behaving as the intrinsic. The reference always treated it as foreign. The declared cascade is one diagnostic because nothing here calls the import: `typeof` on each binding observes that the names exist as bindings without adding a foreign-call or top-level-call rule on top of the module rule. Paired with 17-durable/a-single-action-flow-lowers-to-a-static-plan, which is the same shape on the real specifier.
